Throughput (tokens/sec) is comparable when batching is tuned; core gap appears in cache warmup and routing under multi-tenant noise. transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-08 14:32 PDT | Duration 62m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (AstridCorp Head of ML), Marcus (Platform Eng), Sara (CTO)

Auto-summary: quick recap at top; see action items below.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, sorry about the slight delay, we wanted to get a full lab dump before the call. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Lena: good, thanks. we got the weekly csv, looked at the numbers but i'd love to hear you walk us through the anomalies.
00:12 Jordan: yep, so priya ran the sprint 4 bench overnight and we pulled p50/p95/p99 for short, med, long prompts and compared to your incumbent — caveat, transcription: "incumbent" in sheet as CloudG-ops.
00:25 Priya: quick note, some transcription noise in the logs; there were a couple of cold starts on the quantized variant we tried, so that skewed tail numbers early.
00:34 Marcus: can you call out the numbers? at a glance i see med latencies are close but p99 is worse on Redwood.
00:40 Priya: yes. short prompts (<=32 tokens) median: Redwood 72ms vs baseline 78ms, p95 Redwood 210ms vs baseline 170ms, p99 Redwood 450ms vs baseline 320ms.
00:56 Priya: medium prompts (100-300 tokens) tokens/sec throughput after batching: Redwood 430 tok/s vs baseline 410 tok/s, median latency Redwood 420ms vs baseline 470ms — so we're actually a bit faster median on medium. but tail again is spikier, p95 1.1s vs baseline 900ms.
01:13 Sara: so short median is fine, but those p99 spikes are bad for user experience; what's causing them?
01:19 Priya: main suspects: KV cache cold misses (we saw cache miss rate spike when concurrency ramped), batch windowing misalignment for mixed lengths, and a few outlier queueing events on noisy machines in the multi-tenant pool.
01:30 Jordan: to add, the serving runtime favors continuous batching for cost efficiency; with your burst profile (many short queries then a lull) the aggregator sometimes waits longer to fill a batch which hurts tail.
01:42 Lena: can we tune batch window? i thought you had recommendations to shrink for low-latency services.
01:46 Priya: yes, we suggested adjusting max-batch-wait to 10ms in the config for short prompt paths; we tested 5/10/20ms and 10ms gave best tradeoff. we ran that for the med test and it helped median but didn't fully eliminate p99 spikes.
01:58 Marcus: you mentioned cache prefetch earlier — what would that look like for our workload?
02:03 Priya: two parts: prefix/KV pre-warm for common prompts, and proactive KV warming during deploys. For example, the triage profile shows 12 prompt templates accounting for 62% of requests — we can prime the KV for those at the start of a test.
02:18 Lena: ok. what's the friction for doing a warm-cache steady-state run? we want to know sustained performance, not cold-start drama.
02:24 Jordan: minimal — we can schedule a 30-minute steady-state with warm prefill. we need ephemeral access or dedicated slot so the pool noise is controlled.
02:31 Marcus: about dedicated slots — cost and procurement are the blockers. does Redwood have a 'short-term reserved' option for pilots?
02:38 Jordan: yes, we can provision a temporary dedicated slot for a week under a pilot addendum, cost-estimate in the playbook we'll send. This isolates noisy neighbors and gives a truer head-to-head.
02:46 Sara: sounds good. Does that change any compliance posture? we need to ensure logs and audit trails still flow to our SIEM.
02:52 Jordan: you retain audit logs, and we support pushing logs to your Kinesis/Splunk endpoint; also we already shared SOC2 Type II docs, but i'll resend the redwood security pack with SAML/KMS integration notes.
03:03 Lena: can we pause on fallback strategy — in some tests Redwood fell back to baseline for heavy tails, what policy triggered that?
03:10 Priya: for the pilot we had a conservative timeout threshold at 3s to avoid user-facing waits — requests that crossed that threshold were routed to baseline. We saw an uptick in fallback when p95 crossed 1.2s in some bursts.
03:23 Marcus: so fallback is time-based not token-based? we want more control—prefer cost-based AND latency thresholds.
03:29 Jordan: yep, the routing policy supports multi-dimensional rules: latency threshold, cost ceiling per 1k tokens, region preference. We'll include example rules in the playbook.
03:39 Lena: what about quantization — you tested a 4-bit model, right? any impact?
03:44 Priya: we did; quantized model gave ~18% lower token-cost and similar median latency but slightly higher variance on long-form responses. It's good for throughput but we observed more p99 jitter on long prompts vs FP16. For your workload with many short prompts, quantization looked promising if paired with warm cache.
03:57 Sara: curious — baseline vendor also used quantized variant?
04:01 Priya: baseline was on hybrid configuration; some of their instances had newer tensor cores which reduced variance. hardware differences explain some deltas.
04:09 Jordan: important point: raw latency isn't the only metric — unit-cost and SLA adherence matter. We put together a unit economics sheet comparing tokens per dollar given your traffic; i'll share that.
04:17 Marcus: about instrumentation — we saw mismatch in timestamps across logs (your agent vs our tracing). can we sync on a canonical trace id?
04:23 Priya: yes, we can add a passthrough trace_id header in calls so both sides correlate. we'll include that in the benchmark runner.
04:31 Lena: priya, any quick wins we can flip now before the steady-state run?
04:36 Priya: yes: 1) set max-batch-wait to 10ms for short path, 2) enable prefix caching for top-12 templates, 3) pre-warm KV before test start, 4) pin routing to low-noise pool (or use dedicated slot). Those reduce tail substantially in our lab.
04:50 Jordan: we'll send a short runbook with commands and the config delta; Marcus can apply and we can re-run small-scale before dedicated-run.
04:58 Marcus: ok i'll try to enable prefix caching on Thursday in staging.
05:02 Sara: any risks with enabling prefix cache from a security or PII perspective?
05:07 Jordan: good call — prefix cache should be used with hashed keys and optional TTL; we won't cache raw PII. we'll include guidance and KMS encryption for cached entries.
05:17 Lena: what's the timeline for the dedicated-slot test?
05:20 Jordan: if you provision ephemeral peering creds this week, priya can spin the slot next week (target 2026-09-21); otherwise we can run in multi-tenant with warm-cache earlier.
05:30 Marcus: one more question: how do we verify fallbacks didn't silently change user experience? we need canary metrics.
05:35 Priya: we'll instrument a fallback flag in responses and add a small sampling of end-to-end user flows to check UX. we'll also capture token counts and costs per request.
05:45 Lena: ok great. last thing — can you call out the single biggest blocker for p99?
05:50 Priya: cold KV misses combined with batch alignment under burst — that combination accounts for ~70% of the observed p99 spikes in our traces.
05:58 Jordan: summary: warm-cache steady-state run, tweak batch window, consider dedicated slot if you want clean head-to-head, share security pack, and we'll produce a routing playbook with rule examples.
06:10 Sara: thanks, that helps. let's aim to reconvene after the warm steady run.
06:14 Jordan: perfect. i'll send the playbook and the benchmark template within 24 hours. thanks everyone.
06:20 Lena: thanks all.
06:22 (call ends)
